mainEntity.name: How long should I avoid staining foods after composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally recommended to be most cautious about staining foods and drinks in the first 48 to 72 hours after composite bonding, as the resin surface may be at its most receptive to pigments during this period. After this initial window, sensible ongoing habits — such as rinsing with water after consuming tea, coffee, or red wine — can help maintain the colour match over time. Your dentist will give you specific advice based on your individual treatment.

mainEntity.name: Can I drink coffee after composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coffee is one of the most frequently asked about drinks following composite bonding. It is advisable to avoid it for the first 48 to 72 hours. After that, most patients can resume drinking coffee while taking sensible precautions, such as using a straw where possible, rinsing with water after drinking, and maintaining good oral hygiene. Over time, if noticeable surface staining occurs, a professional polish by your dental hygienist can often improve the appearance.

Composite resin can develop surface and intrinsic staining over time, particularly if heavily pigmented foods and drinks are consumed frequently. Surface staining can often be improved through professional polishing during routine dental appointments. However, deeper discolouration that has penetrated the resin may not be fully reversible with polishing alone, and replacement of the bonding may be considered in some cases. How quickly or significantly staining develops depends on individual dietary habits and oral hygiene.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to eat normally after composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most patients, a return to a normal balanced diet is possible after the initial 48–72 hour period. The main foods worth treating with ongoing care are those that are very hard, very sticky, heavily pigmented, or highly acidic. Maintaining sensible dietary habits and good oral hygiene is generally sufficient to protect the bonding without requiring significant long-term dietary restriction. Your dental team can provide personalised advice based on your specific circumstances.

mainEntity.name: How long does composite bonding last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding typically lasts between five and ten years, though this varies considerably depending on a number of factors including the extent and location of the bonding, individual bite forces, oral hygiene practices, dietary habits, and whether any parafunctional habits such as tooth grinding are present. Individual outcomes cannot be guaranteed. Attending regular dental check-ups allows your dentist to monitor the condition of your bonding and advise on maintenance or replacement when appropriate.

mainEntity.name: Can I have my teeth whitened after composite bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tooth whitening products — whether professional or over-the-counter — do not lighten composite resin. This means that whitening treatments applied after composite bonding is in place may result in your natural teeth brightening while the bonded areas remain the same shade, potentially creating a mismatch in appearance. For this reason, it is generally recommended to undergo any planned whitening treatment before having composite bonding placed, so that the bonding can be matched to your new, whitened shade. Speak with your dental team for individual guidance.
